newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa and U.S. initial new tax treaty.
newsitem.headline: South Africa and U.S. initial new tax treaty.

text.p: South Africa and the U.S. have initialled a treaty aimed at regulating the taxing rights of both countries, Rond van der Merwe, director of legislation at the South African Revenue Services said on Monday.
The treaty, which has still to be checked by legal experts, could be formally signed by the two countries when the U.S.South Africa Binational Commission meets next February, he said.
It will replace a treaty which was terminated in 1986 by the Rangel amendment, which prohibited American companies from using U.S. tax credits for taxes paid in South Africa.
The Rangel amendment was lifted in July 1991 when then U.S. president George Bush lifted trade sanctions against the country.
"This is the new version of the treaty," Van der Merwe said. "The main thrust of it is double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion."
The two parties had agreed not to disclose the terms of the treaty until it was formally signed.
Van der Merwe said the agreement would regulate all types of income taxing rights of the two countries.
"It also allows for credits to be in place between the two tax systems," Van der Merwe said, "and it allows for the extensive exchange of information on tax issues."
